Residents of Agbado-Oke-Odo Local Council Development Area of Lagos State have received business equipment, household appliances and a minibus under a community empowerment initiative organised by the Acting General Manager of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, Olajuwon Akinyemi, in his personal capacity. The beneficiaries received items including sewing machines, generators, grinding machines, hair clippers, chest freezers and foodstuffs at the concluding event of the programme held on Sunday, November 22, at Lemmy Field, Akinola, Aboru, Yana-Ipaja. One resident also received a minibus to start a transport business, in what the organisers described as a special empowerment package. The initiative, tagged ‘Giving Back to the Community’, featured a football competition, a fitness walk, a free medical and eye examination exercise, and the distribution of livelihood-support equipment to residents. Speaking at the event, Akinyemi said the programme was driven by his belief that people who had benefited from the support of their communities had a responsibility to give back, particularly to those who needed assistance. He said the initiative was intended to provide practical support to residents and encourage others with the means to contribute to the development of their communities. “The spirit of giving should be imbibed by everyone. That is my belief, that you should be able to give back to a community that has stood by you all these whiles, through thick and thin,” he said. Akinyemi said he was also inspired by the philanthropic disposition of President Bola Tinubu, whom he described as someone whose goodwill had helped many people. “I am doing this because the President of the country, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, happens to be a giver. He has multitudes of people that his goodwill has brought them so far,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Some beneficiaries said the items would help them expand their small businesses, reduce operating losses and improve their household circumstances. Adijat Abimbola, who received a sewing machine, said the equipment would strengthen her tailoring business and help her earn a better living. “This sewing machine will help me a lot in my handwork, and I am really grateful to the honourable for this gesture,” she said. She also commended the organisers for including medical services in the programme, noting that the health and eye examinations provided an opportunity for residents, including older people, to access basic checks. Another beneficiary, Sumani Olatunji, who received a generator, said he would use it at home to improve his access to electricity. I am really thankful that they gave me this,” he said. A resident identified simply as Ibrahim, who received a chest freezer, said the appliance would help his wife preserve frozen food purchased for resale and prevent losses caused by unsold stock. He explained that his wife bought frozen food in the morning and sold it throughout the day, but items left unsold sometimes went bad because they had no adequate storage facility. “My wife goes out in the morning to buy frozen foods and sells them for hours till evening. Sometimes, we have leftovers which go to waste and reduce profit or even at times leave her at a loss. “I believe we can use the freezer in this regard. It will boost our business,” he said. The initiative also attracted political and community leaders, including the Chairman of Onigbongbo Local Council Development Area, Moyo Adebanjo, who commended Akinyemi for directing personal resources towards supporting residents. Adebanjo said the intervention demonstrated a commitment to the community and could help restore hope among residents facing economic difficulties. “What Mr Juwon Akinyemi has done is highly impressive, and this speaks to the fact that he is a genuine community member, someone who, out of his own little resources, has decided to reward members of the community who are lacking in one way or the other and, of course, rekindle their hope in the party,” he said. Akinyemi also emphasised the importance of initiatives that support people at the grassroots, saying they offered opportunities to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. A representative of Atlantic Briscoe Construction, Remilekun Durojaiye, described the intervention as commendable and urged other stakeholders to support similar efforts in their communities. He said initiatives that directly address the needs of residents could complement wider development programmes by providing practical assistance to households and small businesses. The programme’s activities began with a two-kilometre fitness walk and football competition on November 14, followed by the third-place match and final on November 20. A free medical outreach, including general health and eye examinations, was held on November 21, before the empowerment exercise the following day. The organisers said the combination of sports, healthcare and material support was intended to reach residents across different age groups and address needs beyond financial assistance. For beneficiaries such as Abimbola and Ibrahim, however, the immediate value of the intervention lies in the equipment they can now put to work: a sewing machine to support a trade and a freezer to protect the earnings of a small business.
